newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - De Beers set for record CSO sales.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - De Beers set for record CSO sales.

text.p: Rough diamond sales by De Beers' Central Selling Organisation are set to reach record levels in 1996, mainly on the back of strong U.S. demand.
De Beers will announce the full-year sales figure on Wednesday with analysts predicting a solid rise to between $4.80-$4.95 billion from $4.53 billion in 1995.
"They've got a lot going for them," said James Picton, analyst at Standard Equities in South Africa.
Besides the U.S., De Beers will probably also be enjoying good growth in new markets such as India, Pakistan and Turkey, Picton added.
De Beers sells rough diamonds to a select group of dealers at so-called "sights", which take place 10 times per year. The last time was last week.
Sales will also have grown due to increased demand from the Far East, but the rise will still have been smaller than in the first half of the 1990s, analysts said.
Overall sales growth may have been dampened slightly by the decision in June by Australia's Argyle mine to pull out of the CSO and start marketing its stones on its own.
Roger Chaplin at T. Hoare & Co in London believes this may have cost De Beers $100 to $150 million.

A recent increase in Russian sales outside the CSO may also have prompted the organisation to hold back supply to diamond cutters to keep prices stable, said analyst Charles Kernot at Paribas Capital Markets.
But he reckons the Russian "leakages" were mainly aimed at financing regional elections and expects these sales to stop once the elections have taken place later this month.
"It (the leakage) is not massive and it seems temporary," Kernot said.
Political turmoil has meanwhile delayed a new diamond marketing deal between De Beers and Russia and analysts said it was completely unclear when or whether a deal may be reached.
"It is completely fluid," said Des Mayers at brokers G. O'Flaherty in Johannesburg.
But all analysts agree the current situation is stable enough not to harm De Beers.
